text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- James Baker, United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara, says he sees no solution this year on the deadlock over a planned referendum for the region despite some progress.
- Japan's parliamentary vice-president starts visit to Morocco.
- Marrakesh to host five-day international railway seminar starting October 6.
- Health workers unions call for a three day strike starting July 22 following failure of previous strikes.
- London's meeting on referendum in Western Sahara marks important step towards a solution to crisis.
- Nurses live below poverty line on only 2,500 dirhams ($257.7) monthly.
